questions.prompt: How should the phase bar on top of a workspace render?
questions.context: Mocks for every option are on this page under “Phase bar”. The first three were requested; the rest come from stepper guidance in common design systems.

options.label: Extended — name, index and deliverable
options.description: Current. The deliverable subline is the only place the phase outcome is written down.

options.label: Minimal — name and index
options.description: Same chevrons and hues, no subline; a prop on the existing component.

options.label: Vertical — chevron stack beside the action bar
options.description: No top row; the stack sits on the left of the action bar, the branch chip leaves this row.
options.risks: Needs a new layout slot in the ribbon row.

options.label: Vertical, tall — chevron column, one big icon each
options.description: Left column, one big icon per chevron.
options.tradeoffs: Takes 180px of width from the content pane.

options.label: Progress tracker — dots and names
options.description: Classic stepper; reads as linear progress rather than navigation.

options.label: Segmented tabs — underlined
options.description: Lowest height of the full-name options.
options.risks: Looks like tabs, which may suggest free switching.

options.label: Compact — current phase pill
options.description: One pill with a menu and a three-segment progress mark.
options.risks: Other phases are not visible without opening it.

options.label: Vertical list — stepper in the left column
options.description: Plain stepper list in a left column; nothing renders on top.

options.label: Hidden — phase shown in the action bar tail
options.description: For people who only need the actions.

questions.prompt: How should the action bar under the phase bar render?
questions.context: Mocks for every option are on this page under “Action bar”. The first four were requested; the rest come from Office's simplified ribbon and Fluent's command-bar guidance.

options.label: Extended icons — icon, label, group caption
options.description: The UXv2 look, Office style.
options.tradeoffs: Tallest; scrolls horizontally in a narrow pane.

options.label: Minimal icons — icon only, label on hover
options.risks: Several built-ins share a verb today (two Approval actions, two Preview actions).

options.label: Extended text — group headers and text buttons
options.description: Current. Group headers carry the phase vocabulary.

options.label: Minimal text — text buttons, no headers
options.description: Current buttons, headers removed, groups separated by dividers.

options.label: Simplified — one row, icon + label, overflow menu
options.description: Office's simplified ribbon; most legible of the compact ones.

options.label: Icon rail — frequent actions only, rest in a menu
options.description: Fluent command bar.

options.label: Menu bar — each group is a dropdown
Collapsed — primary action and an Actions menu
options.description: The equivalent of Office's auto-hide ribbon.

questions.prompt: When I switch workspace tabs and come back, what must still be there?
questions.context: PR #380 keeps one mounted workspace page: saved state (open documents, phase, timeline) comes back, running state (an unsent chat draft, scroll position, an open dialog) does not. The mock kept every tab mounted in its own iframe.

options.label: What I was looking at is enough (PR #380 as is)
options.description: Open center tabs, phase and timeline are restored; a draft and the scroll position start over.

options.label: Also keep my draft and my place in the timeline
options.description: Save the unsent chat text and the scroll position per workspace, the same way the open tabs are saved.
options.tradeoffs: Small follow-up; still one page, one connection.

options.label: Keep every open workspace fully alive
options.description: Instant switching with everything intact, like the mock.
options.risks: N sockets, N agent streams, N× memory; the page was never built to run several times at once.

questions.prompt: Does the Oct 6 UI meeting override the September prompts wherever they conflict?
questions.context: The UX v2 plan was written from the Oct 6 meeting. In six places it says the opposite of what a prompt asked (C1–C6 below). If the meeting wins, the plan must say so item by item; if not, three contradictions are presentation-only and cheap to absorb now.

options.label: Yes — the meeting wins; label each dropped prompt V2 explicitly
No — the prompts stand; absorb the cheap contradictions now
Decide item by item (vote on C1–C6 below)

questions.prompt: C1 · Left rail: one “Issues & tasks” item with Activity on top, or the plan's Tasks + Issues?
questions.context: Prompts #24 and #26 asked for Activity at the very top and no distinction between issues and tasks. Phase 0 (merged) orders the rail project-docs, ontology, files, tasks, issues with no Activity entry; PR #406's rail (screenshot) already shows Activity on top and one Issues & tasks item.

options.label: Activity, docs, ontology, files, Issues & tasks (one item); Jobs labelled V2
Keep the plan's rail (Tasks and Issues separate, no Activity entry)

questions.prompt: C2 · Integration Engineering ribbon: add the shared Author and Analysis group?
questions.context: Prompt #26: “New doc and import and analyze should be in each ribbon.” The plan's IE button set is Approval, Create PR and rebase, Merge to parent only; PR #406 already renders the shared group in IE (screenshot).

options.label: Add New doc, Import, Analyze, Review meeting to IE (config only)
Keep IE to its release actions

questions.prompt: C3 · Home rows: colour the Open button, or show status badges?
questions.context: Prompts #46 and #51: the Open button's colour is the status (red waiting for input, blue working, white idle), remove the tags. The plan shows needs-input / working badges plus a fourth “unknown” state.

options.label: Colour the Open button; no badges; unknown renders white
Keep the plan's badges with the unknown state

questions.prompt: C4 · Review meeting decisions: do Accept and Delay create tasks?
questions.context: Prompt #48: Accept creates a task the agent implements immediately; Delay creates a task too; decisions get marked implemented afterwards (#35). The plan only writes a status (accepted, delayed, out of scope, rejected) to the decisions document, and the meeting said “no local issues” in V1.

options.label: Local tasks in V1: Accept and Delay create a task
V1 writes a status only; add “implemented” to the status list and say Accept creates no task

questions.prompt: C5 · Activity: the primary issue's conversation with a composer, or a platform-event feed that links out?
questions.context: Prompt #26: the workspace activity log is the primary issue page, tracker comments and workspace events interleaved, posting as the person to the tracker. The plan builds a timeline of platform events that references, never duplicates, issue discussion. PR #406's timeline (screenshot on this page) already interleaves issue discussion and carries a composer, so the vote is whether that stays V1 or the plan's wording wins.

options.label: Tracker comments and a composer in the landing timeline (V1)
Platform-event feed that links to the issue; the issue-page shape is V2

questions.prompt: C6 · Deployment plan with rollback knobs versus “IE ends at merge”
questions.context: Prompt #26 asked for a Deployment plan / Knobs template covering how to turn features off. The phases decision says IE ends at merge with no production deployment or monitoring, yet the V2 backlog keeps “Deployment plan”. Planning is not deploying.

options.label: Reword the phases decision to allow planning documents; deployment itself stays out of scope
Drop the Deployment plan entry from the V2 backlog

questions.prompt: Which of the five asked-for-but-unlabelled items should move into V1? (pick any)
questions.context: The plan says everything else in the mock is labelled V2, but these five are in neither list. The workspace Issues & tasks panel is already built in PR #406 (screenshots on this page), so picking it keeps it; unpicked items go to the V2 backlog explicitly.

options.label: Jobs panel (running processes, running chats)
Import ontology · Link ontology in the Import menu
User stories active doc (create tasks; create tasks and implement)
Workspace Issues & tasks panel (quick-add, Action menu, Import task picker, mark done)
Project docs icons and out-of-date indicators

questions.prompt: Review experience: how should overview, timeline, changes and approvals be laid out?
questions.context: From the 2026-10-09 standup. Rahul's prototype has four review tabs; James and Ben pointed at GitHub, where everything sits in one conversation stream; Ben also floated filters over one timeline, and a fourth top-level tab for review; Davide suggested ribbon buttons beside New doc / Import / Analyze. Rahul is already reducing four tabs toward one and keeps Changes separate. Wireframes of each option are on this page.

options.label: Four tabs — Overview, Timeline, Changes, Approvals (the prototype)
options.description: Each concern on its own tab; the timeline merges workspace events and PR activity.
options.risks: Side tabs plus top tabs read as too many tabs (Ziniu); a third of the screen is chrome (James).

options.label: One timeline with filters, Changes as the one separate tab
options.description: Overview on top of the timeline, approvals and reports interleaved, filters by phase and approval; the diff stays its own tab.
options.tradeoffs: Closest to a GitHub pull request; the existing Activity page becomes this timeline.

options.label: Review views as ribbon buttons beside New doc / Import / Analyze
options.description: Timeline, Changes and Approvals open from the action bar; personalisable.
options.risks: More buttons in a ribbon that reviewers cannot use ("chaos central").

options.label: A fourth top-level Review tab
options.description: Review is its own surface next to the phases, with the ribbon out of the way.
options.risks: Diverges from one unified view for owner and reviewers.

questions.prompt: Center pane: keep document tabs, or drop them and rely on the sidebar and browser tabs?
questions.context: From the 2026-10-09 standup. QA keeps a center pane with tabs (Chat, Activity, each open document). Tim's mock has none: you switch documents from the sidebar. Ziniu: tabs are still needed for several ontology nodes or documents; James: decide once, no setting; Davide: hide them for a while and see if we miss them. A real screenshot of today's center tabs is on this page.

options.label: Keep center pane tabs
options.description: Several documents or ontology nodes open at once, switched in place.
options.tradeoffs: A row of chrome in every workspace.

options.label: Drop them: one document at a time, sidebar and browser tabs do the rest
options.description: Tim's model as drawn.
options.risks: Comparing two specs means two browser tabs or the sidebar every time.

options.label: Hide them now, keep the backend notion, revisit after the friction logs
options.description: Cheapest reversible step; decide for good next week.

questions.prompt: Keep the workspace tabs across the top of the app?
questions.context: From the 2026-10-09 standup. The strip (already in QA) comes from Tim's mocks so you switch workspaces inside G5 instead of juggling Chrome tabs; Ben: it helps tell workspaces apart when many are open; Ziniu and Zhengchun questioned its value. Screenshot on this page.

options.label: Keep the workspace tabs
options.tradeoffs: One row at the very top; per-workspace restore is already in PR #380.

options.label: Drop them; the workspace switcher and Home are enough
options.risks: Back to one Chrome tab per workspace.

questions.prompt: May a reviewer use a running preview on someone else's workspace?
questions.context: From the 2026-10-09 standup. Starting a preview is a modifying operation on the owner's VM (it can crash a workspace mid-compile) and a preview that reads or writes the VM can leak its secrets to whoever uses it. Ziniu: business alignment needs everyone in the same preview; Ben: a 20-minute preview should be started once and shared; Rahul: viewing in your own fork is cleaner. Agreed direction: read access to the workspace gates access to its running preview, some day.

options.label: Only the owner starts a preview; anyone who can read the workspace may use it
options.risks: Preview secrets are the owner's responsibility.

options.label: Reviewers fork and start their own preview
options.risks: Database state may differ; no shared session for alignment.

options.label: Only the owner sees the preview
options.risks: No collaborative review of a running preview.
